{{nihongo|'''Oo Shrine'''|大神社 (一宮市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Oo Shrine''' (おおじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Yamato-chō Oho|ja|大和町於保|qid=Q126900259}} (Oho), {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=old ranking}} is {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines one {{ill|Column|an|Columna (arquitectura)|ar|عمود (إنشاء)|az|Sütun|bcl|Harigi|be|Калона|be_x_old|Калёна|bg|Колона|bh|थम|bn|স্তম্ভ|br|Kolonenn|bs|Stub|ca|Columna|ckb|کۆڵەکە|cs|Sloup (architektura)|da|Søjle|de|Säule|el|Κίονας|eo|Kolono|es|Columna (arquitectura)|et|Sammas|eu|Zutabe|fa|ستون|fi|Pylväs|fr|Colonne (architecture)|ga|Colún|gl|Columna (arquitectura)|he|עמוד|hi|स्तम्भ|hr|Stup|hu|Oszlop|id|Tonggak|it|Colonna|ja|柱|kk|Колонна|kn|ಕಂಬ|ko|기둥|ky|Колонна|la|Columna|lfn|Colona|li|Zuul (boewkunde)|lt|Kolona|lv|Kolonna|mk|Столб|ml|തൂൺ|ms|Turus|mzn|کلونا|ne|थाम|new|थां|nl|Zuil (bouwkunde)|nn|Søyle|no|Søyle|nrm|Colonne|oc|Colona (arquitectura)|pl|Kolumna (architektura)|pnb|تھملا|pt|Coluna|qu|Tunu|ro|Coloană|ru|Колонна|sah|Колонна|scn|Culonna|sco|Column|sd|ٿنبو|sh|Stup|simple|Column|sk|Stĺp|sl|Steber|sn|Mbiru|sq|Kolona (arkitekturë)|sr|Стуб|su|Kolom|sv|Kolonn (arkitektur)|sw|Nguzo|ta|தூண்|te|స్తంభం|tg|Сутун|th|เสา|tl|Haligi|tr|Kolon|uk|Колона|ur|ستون (عمارت)|uz|Ustun|vi|Cột trụ|vls|Piloare|wuu|柱|zh|柱|zh_yue|柱|qid=Q4817}}:
* '''{{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}}''' (かむやいみみのみこと) - a {{ill|Imperial Prince|ja|皇子|ko|황자|vi|Hoàng tử|zh|皇子|zh_min_nan|Hông-chú|qid=Q12886381}} of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}} (1st emperor), ancestor of the {{ill|Ō clan|ja|多氏|qid=Q11430816}}.

Some sources say Hachiōji is enshrined in the aiden, which is said to derive from this shrine being called "Tennō-sha" in the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
Founding is unknown. As seen in both shrine and place names, it is said the {{ill|Ō clan|ja|多氏|qid=Q11430816}} (Ōuji), who lived here, enshrined their ancestral deity {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}} as clan tutelary deity{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}. This clan was an ancient lineage based around Oho-gō in {{ill|Toichi district|ja|十市郡|zh|十市郡|qid=Q11405036}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}} (present {{ill|Tawaramoto, Nara|arz|تاواراموتو|ceb|Tawaramoto-chō (subdistrito)|es|Tawaramoto (Nara)|fa|تاواراموتو، نارا|fr|Tawaramoto|hy|Տավարամոտո|it|Tawaramoto|ja|田原本町|ko|다와라모토정|mg|Tawaramoto|ms|Tawaramoto, Nara|my|တဝရမိုတိုမြို့၊ နာရ|pl|Tawaramoto|ru|Таварамото|sv|Tawaramoto|tl|Tawaramoto, Nara|tr|Tawaramoto|uk|Таварамото|ur|ٹاوارا موٹو، نارا|zh|田原本町|qid=Q1203159}}, {{ill|Shiki District, Nara|ar|شيكي|ca|Districte de Shiki|ceb|Shiki-gun|es|Distrito de Shiki|fr|District de Shiki|id|Distrik Shiki, Nara|it|Distretto di Shiki|ja|磯城郡|ko|시키군|nl|Shiki (Nara)|pl|Powiat Shiki|ru|Сики (уезд)|simple|Shiki District, Nara|zh|磯城郡|qid=Q1155036}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}), where their tutelary {{ill|Oonimasumishiritsuhiko Shrine|ja|多坐弥志理都比古神社|qid=Q11430652}} (also called Ō Shrine; a Shikinaisha Myojin-taisha) is located.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|cs|Rikkokuši|de|Rikkokushi|es|Rikkokushi|eu|Rikkokushi|fa|شش تاریخ ملی|fr|Rikkokushi|it|Rikkokushi|ja|六国史|ko|육국사|pt|Rikkokushi|ru|Риккокуси|simple|Rikkokushi|zh|六國史|qid=Q1151168|lt=official histories}}, in {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} 3 ({{ill|853|Q30367|qid=Q30367}}) "Ō tenjin" is listed as a myojin, and in the same year was given {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} Junior Fifth Upper; then in {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1 ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), "Ō myojin" was promoted to Senior Fifth Upper{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}<ref>In '{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}},' Kaśhō 3 (850), 9th month, day 26, "Owari Ō Shrine" appears; a theory identifies this with Oo Shrine, but it is generally identified with {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065}} {{Harv|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}.</ref>.

Also, in the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), under {{ill|Nakashima district|Q780420|qid=Q780420}}, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, it is listed as "Ō Shrine, Myojin-tai," and ranked as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}. In manuscript copies the name is written both "Ōgami Shrine" and "Ōkamisha," but in that case one "神" character is treated as an interpolation{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}. In the Engishiki temporary-festival myojin-festival section it also says: "Ō Shrine one seat, alternatively written Ta-sakuta," indicating a form "Ta Shrine." Because the place name "Oho" has long remained in this area, these entries are taken to refer to this shrine{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}. In the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wamyōshō}},' this area is identified with Kawasaki-gō, Nakajima District{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}.

Later details are unclear. It is said to have declined as clan members scattered, and by the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} it was called "Tennō-sha"{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was ranked {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}{{Sfn|太神神社（式内社）|1989年}}. Today, its chief priest concurrently serves several shrines, including {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine, Ichinomiya|Q546197|qid=Q546197|lt=Ōgami Shrine}} in Ichinomiya.
